title: Goal calculations are inaccurate
scope: Live dev environment (https://dev.salesplanning.ingka.com, retail unit US), real backend data from https://api.dev.salesplanning.ingka.com/metrics. 211 entities probed: 1 country, 19 HFBs, 191 product areas. This run confirms the reporter’s description — it is not an independent claim.
repro:
Everything below is read live in one browser session. No tooling beyond DevTools and a calculator.

Setup (do this once)

  1. Open https://dev.salesplanning.ingka.com/region-dashboard/us and sign in.
  2. Open DevTools → Network tab, and type metrics into the filter box.
  3. Reload the page.
  4. Click the POST request to api.dev.salesplanning.ingka.com/metrics whose Payload is {"metric":"KPI_SUMMARY","level":"hfb","filters":{"retailUnitCode":"US"}}.
  5. Open its Response tab. Under data.children you get one entry per HFB. Every number is a string in Java scientific notation — "3.3198394048E8" means 331983940.48.

A. The gap is measured against the FULL-YEAR goal

  1. In the response, find the child whose hfbNo is 01 (Living room seating).
  2. Read three fields: netQuantityYtd = 2,049,167, netQuantityGoalFy = 2,032,719, netQuantityGap = −16,448.
  3. On a calculator: 2,032,719 − 2,049,167 = −16,448.
  4. That is netQuantityGap exactly. So gap = goalFy − ytd. It holds on all 210 entities that returned data.

B. The index is measured against the YEAR-TO-DATE goal

  1. Same HFB 01 child. Read netQuantityGoalYtd = 1,890,972 and netQuantityIndexToGoal = 108.37.
  2. On a calculator: 2,049,167 ÷ 1,890,972 × 100 = 108.37.
  3. That is netQuantityIndexToGoal exactly. So index = ytd ÷ goalYtd × 100.
  4. Compare with step A: the gap divides against GoalFy, the index against GoalYtd. Two different denominators. That is why the two numbers can contradict each other on the same card.

C. The "Gap to close" line is shown on exactly the wrong cards

  1. Go back to https://dev.salesplanning.ingka.com/region-dashboard/us and scroll to the HFB cards.
  2. Count how many cards show a Gap to close line. The answer is 2 of 19: HFB 01 Living room seating (16K / $72.2M) and HFB 10 Lighting & Home electronics (201K / $49.8M).
  3. Now look up those two in the API response. HFB 01 netQuantityGap = −16,448; HFB 10 netQuantityGap = −201,122. Both are negative — they have already passed the full-year goal, so there is nothing left to close.
  4. Now pick any card with no Gap to close line, e.g. HFB 17 Outdoor. Its netQuantityGap is +607,063 and its index is 73.46 — it is genuinely a long way behind, and it is exactly the card that should be showing a gap.
  5. Check the sign against the display for all 19 HFBs. The line appears if and only if the gap is negative, with zero exceptions. The condition is inverted.
  6. Also note the two shown values are the absolute value of a negative number: HFB 01’s −16,448 is rendered as 16K.

D. The reported symptom, in the reporter’s own words

  1. Switch the HFB list toggle to Sales index.
  2. Take HFB 05 Beds & Mattresses: the card shows an index of 83.66 (well below 100) and no Gap to close — which reads as "we met the target".
  3. In the API response its netSalesGap is −44,511,343: negative, because YTD sales already exceed the full-year sales goal, even though YTD sales are 16% short of the year-to-date goal.
  4. That is the exact contradiction on the ticket. It reproduces on 17 of the 19 HFBs.

E. The underlying data problem: FY goal is smaller than YTD goal

  1. Still in the same HFB response, read HFB 01’s netSalesGoalFy = 259,773,463 and netSalesGoalYtd = 360,633,550.
  2. The full-year goal is smaller than the goal due by week 34. For a cumulative target that is impossible — the whole year cannot be less than part of the year.
  3. Repeat for the other HFBs: all 19 have GoalFy < GoalYtd, ratio 0.71–0.85.
  4. Now change the request body to {"metric":"KPI_SUMMARY","level":"pa","filters":{"retailUnitCode":"US","hfbNo":"01"}} and check the product areas: their ratio is ~1.04 and none are inverted. The quantity goals are also fine. The defect is specific to HFB-level sales goals.

Open question (not established)

At week 34 of 52 you would expect GoalFy ÷ GoalYtd to be roughly 1.5. HFBs show ~0.72 and product areas show ~1.04. Neither matches clean pro-rating, so the goal-loading rule itself is not something this run can explain — it needs someone who knows how GoalFy and GoalYtd are populated upstream.
